classification.difficultyReason: Identify the hypotenuse from the right-angle diagram, form a Pythagorean equation with algebraic side lengths, solve the quadratic and reject geometrically invalid lengths.

content.prompt:
Find the value of $x$ in the diagram.

Introduce a pronumeral, write down a quadratic equation and solve it.

spec.sourceRegion: Exercise 17D question 5, triangle to the right of the prompt
spec.description: Right triangle with vertical left leg, horizontal bottom leg, descending hypotenuse and a right-angle square at the lower-left vertex. Ordinary source blue strokes are reconstructed in house black.
spec.mathematics: Legs (x+1) cm and (2x+4) cm; hypotenuse (3x+1) cm.
spec.answerVisibility: All three algebraic lengths and the right-angle marker are permanent givens; no solution value appears.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the pronumeral shown. By Pythagoras,
$$\begin{align*}(x+1)^2+(2x+4)^2&=(3x+1)^2\\x^2+2x+1+4x^2+16x+16&=9x^2+6x+1\\5x^2+18x+17&=9x^2+6x+1\\4x^2-12x-16&=0\\x^2-3x-4&=0\\(x-4)(x+1)&=0\\x-4&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x+1=0\\x&=4\quad\text{or}\quad x=-1\end{align*}$$
Reject $x=-1$, since it gives a zero leg and a negative hypotenuse. Therefore $x=4$.

Check: the side lengths are $5\text{ cm}$, $12\text{ cm}$ and $13\text{ cm}$, and $5^2+12^2=13^2$.
